questions.question: Are any of the plaintiff's attorneys included in the list of attorneys bad actors?
questions.expectedAnswer: Yes — plaintiff's attorney Silberstein, Awad & Miklos, P.C. is flagged as a bad-actor attorney.

questions.question: Is there any evidence of irregular procedures or violations in the plaintiff's case pertaining to workers compensation rules and regulations?
Is the plaintiff's address included in the list of known fraud claimants addresses?
Did plaintiff claim lost wages upon retaining counsel, but returned to work shortly after the accident?
Display Question: Is there evidence that the plaintiff was identified by the ISO or NICB as a fraud risk red flag?
Is there evidence that the plaintiff's was identified by the ISO or NICB as having had 2 or more claims over the last 3 years?
Are any of the plaintiff's medical providers included in the list of medical providers bad actors?
Do several plaintiff's medical providers share the same specifc address?

Is there evidence that other people were present at the side of the accident and allegedly witnessed the accident  but yet no one formally confirmed the plaintiff's accident account in deposition or written statement?
Was the plaintiff's accident reported to a supervisor?
Was the plaintiff not admitted to the hospital on the day of his first visit to the ER but received subsequent treatments for a period longer than 12 weeks?
Did the plaintiff's medical condition not improve after 45 days of treatment?

Is the period of time between the date of the accident and the earliest date plaintiff sought treatment conducted after the initial ER visit unexpectedly long given the plaintiff's medical findings by medical providers?
Is there any evidence that pre-existing medical conditions or prior injuries could be a factor in plaintiff's medical reports?

Are there inconsistencies between the plaintiff's initial medical findings from the ER doctors and the the plaintiff's medical findings from plaintiff's doctors after the plaintiff's initial ER visit?
Was the plaintiffs description of the cause of the injury inconsistent with the ER medical findings?
Was there clear medical evidence that the plaintiff's medical conditions and findings in the ER would result in the subsequent medical treatments?
Was there clear medical evidence that the plaintiff's medical conditions and findings in the ER would result in the subsequent surgery?
Was the plaintiff not admitted to the hospital on the day of his first visit to the ER on or after the day of the accident but was deemed 100% Disabled by evaluating doctors in the lawsuit?
Is the plaintiff over 35 years of age? If so, were there mention of the word degenerative in any medical reports and MRI or x-ray findings by plaintiff's medical providers?
What was the plaintiff's pain rating and what was his blood pressure and heart rate at the ER and are these findings inconsistent with the pain rating table of blood pressure and heart beats data?
Is there social postings evidence that the plaintiff's life and physical activities that would contradict plaintiff's claim of disability?
Did the plaintiffs description of the cause of the injury evolve over time?
Was the plaintiff's original description of the cause of the injury unrelated to New York, Labor Law 240 implications but subsequent description became relevant to that law and its consequences?
Was the plaintiff's original description of the cause of the injury unrelated to New York, Labor Law 241 implications but subsequent description became relevant to that law and its consequences?
Did plaintiff's diagnosis gets worse over time and include injuries to parts of body not reported when first sought care after the accident?
Did the plaintiff statements in deposition contradict the accident witnesses statements?

Did the plaintiff develop increasingly frequent non-verifiable medical conditions like vertigo, headache, PTSD, anxiety, Phobias, insomnia, and other psychological conditions over weeks and months following the accident?
Is there any evidence that plaintiff did not remember any of the doctors or locations or clinics where he received treatment for this accident?
Did the date of plaintiff injury occur within 30 days of his first day on the job site where the accident happened?
Is there photographic or video evidence that the plaintiff showing no signs of impairments or reduced physical capabilities that would contradict plaintiff's claim of disability?
Did plaintiff retained legal counsel to represent this case on his behalf within 30 days of the accident?
Did the plaintiff retain legal counsel to represent him in this case prior than seeking further medical attention susbsequent to the ER visit?
Is there evidence of how plaintiff's obtained legal counsel to represent this case on his behalf?
Is there any evidence that the plaintiff began treatments with his current medical providers because he followed the instructions of his attorneys?
